PaperBanana: AI for Analysis and Review of Scientific Articles

The video features PaperBanana, a system of Google AI agents with the University of Beijing that generates illustrations for scientific articles from the text of the methodology. Explains the gargal of the figures, the team of five agents (Retriever, Planner, Stylist, Visualizer and Critic), the benchmark PaperBananaBench and what this automation changes in scientific work.

  • AI tools
  • Agentic engineering

The neck of scientific illustrations

For those who research, one of the most frustrating tasks is to transform complex ideas into clear illustrations to publish an article. The video features PaperBanana, a tool that promises to deliver this work to an AI 00:00.

A quality diagram, such as the best publications, can take days or weeks from a specialist designer 00:22. The promise is to generate such an illustration from scratch, from a simple text 00:43.

The script goes through the illustration bottleneck, PaperBanana and his team of agents, the tests and what this automation means for science 00:43.

The article itself calls the task of laborious neck: weeks drawing a diagram are weeks less for the next discovery 01:25.

Current tools don't solve. The code is rigid and limits creativity; image generators do beautiful things, but hardly ever have the technical precision that an article requires 01:25. A bridge between the two worlds was missing 01:46.

A team of agents

PaperBanana was developed by researchers from Google and Beijing University as an assistant focused on this task. 02:08.

He's not a single model trying to do everything. It is an agent framework, such as an assembly line: each agent has a function and passes the work to the next 02:08.

The researcher provides the text of the methodology and the caption he wants for the figure 02:50. The flow has two phases 03:10:

1. Planning: AI decides what to illustrate and how to 03:10. 2. Refining: AI creates a first version and reviews it in cycles. According to the video, it's three rounds 03:10.

Team members 03:31:

  • Retriever, the research intern, who seeks good examples as reference 03:31.
  • Planner, the architect, who draws the skeleton of the figure 03:31.
  • Stylist, the art director, who defines the look 03:31.
  • Visualizer, the illustrator, drawing 03:31.
  • Critic, quality control, which reviews, points errors and returns for adjustment 03:53.

The tests

To evaluate the system, the team created PaperBananaBench: 292 diagrams of published scientific articles, which the AI tried to recreate with the same quality 04:14.

According to the video, in the overall quality assessment PaperBanana surpassed the other methods by 17% 04:14. The highest gain, of more than 37%, was in the concision: the AI seeks the most clear and direct way to communicate the idea 04:36. The project page states that the method surpasses competitors in fidelity, concision, legibility and aesthetics, without giving the percentages in the text.

The system is versatile: it generates from methodology flowcharts to statistical graphs for data visualization 04:58.

Automate the scientist

The point goes beyond convenience. Automate a task that consumes so much time frees researchers to research, innovate and discover, and accelerates science as a whole 05:39.

The video summarizes three contributions 06:01:

1. The framework, which shows that this automation is possible 06:01. 2. PaperBananaBench, a quality ruler for the community 06:01. 3. The proof that the team approach surpasses what existed before 06:01.

The final question: If the machine can already visualize science, the human role may be to ask the right questions. Where are we gonna point the curiosity? 06:22

Frequently Asked Questions

What does PaperBanana generate?

Illustrations for scientific articles, such as methodology diagrams and statistical graphs, from the text of the methodology and the legend of the figure 02:50.

How does PaperBanana guarantee the quality of the figure?

With a critical agent, which compares the result with the request, points errors and returns the figure for adjustment in refinement cycles 03:53.

Fonts

  • PaperBanana: Automating Academic Illustration for AI ScientistsProject page, researchers from the University of Beijing and Google Cloud AI Research. It describes a framework of agents that generates academic illustrations ready for publication: it seeks references, plans content and style, renders and refines by self-criticism. Names Retriever, Planner, Stylist, Visualizer and Critic agents; features PaperBananaBench, with 292 cases of testing methodology diagrams taken from NeurIPS 2025 articles; and shows that the method also generates statistical graphs.

Reviewed by Maurício Yokoyama Issei in 19 November 2026.

About the video

In this video you will know PaperBanana, an innovative tool based on Artificial Intelligence designed to support the reading, analysis and understanding of scientific articles.

If you are a researcher, student or professional working with academic production, this solution can significantly optimize your time at:

✔️ Resumir artigos técnicos
Highlight main contributions
✔️ Identificar limitações e pontos fortes
✔️ Facilitar a compreensão de conteúdos complexos

PaperBanana uses advanced language models to transform the scientific review experience, making the process more agile and strategic.

Access the official project here:
https://dwzhu-pku.github.io/PaperBanana/
